function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to check if Chrome is installed. We need to use the provided tool to run a command. On Windows, we can check if chrome.exe exists in Program Files or Program Files (x86). We can use where command: "where chrome.exe" or "where google-chrome.exe"? On Windows, Chrome is usually installed at C:\Program Files (x86)\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe or C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe. We can use "where chrome.exe" which will search PATH. But Chrome may not be in PATH. Alternatively, we can check registry or existence of file. But simplest: use "where chrome.exe" and see if it returns path. If not found, we can try "where google-chrome.exe". But the question: "is chrome is installed". We can respond with a command that checks existence. Use "cmd_controller_execute" with command "where chrome.exe". That will return path if found. If not found, we can say not installed. But we can't parse output. We can just run "where chrome.exe" and let the system output. But we might want to check existence via "if exist". For example: "if exist \"C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe\" echo Chrome installed". But we don't know exact path. We can use "where /q chrome.exe" to suppress output and exit code indicates presence. But we can't capture exit code. So maybe just run "where chrome.exe" and let the output show path. That is fine.

Thus we call the function with command "where chrome.exe".
